name: rr-chip
summary: Outlined uppercase chip naming a discrete thing — a category, skill or filter. The square, transparent counterpart to the filled badge.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Chip label text. Rendered uppercase via CSS — pass normal-case text.

guidance: Chip vs badge is a question of provenance, not interactivity. A badge reports state the system decided and you cannot influence — status, count, validity. A chip names a discrete thing — a category, a skill, a filter, a value someone chose. Pick by asking who decided what it says, not by whether it is clickable.
The visual split follows from that: the chip is outlined (transparent fill, square radius.sm), the badge is a filled pill.

Do not point a chip border at --color-border-default: it equals background.alt and disappears on the page canvas. The default variant uses foreground.muted and the subtle variant uses border.elevated so both stay visible standalone.
Content is transformed to uppercase with --letter-spacing-all-caps in CSS; authors pass normal-case text and must not pre-uppercase it.

This element is the STATIC chip and exposes no role. A chip may legitimately be interactive — a filter that toggles, a removable value, a trigger that opens a listbox — but those modes are not built yet (#229). Until they are, compose an interactive chip from rr-button or rr-link; do not attach handlers to this host.

When a chip is used as the trigger for a popup, it must not declare aria-haspopup or aria-expanded itself. The popup stamps those onto whatever sits in its trigger slot, exactly as rr-menu already does — so the same chip stays correct when it is used as a plain filter.

rules: Chip text alone must convey meaning; do not rely on the border or emphasis level to communicate.
This element is a static label — not focusable, no role. Interactive chips are composed from rr-button or rr-link until the interactive modes land (#229).
Both variants meet WCAG AA for text contrast on the base canvas (default 8.0:1, subtle 6.3:1).
